title: reference-impl v0.6.2 — leftover dogfood debt
problem:
# Brief: reference-impl v0.6.2 — leftover dogfood debt

The v0.6.1 walker correctness patch line shipped 2026-04-27 (Plan CLV-33,
6 tasks merged, final HEAD `580bec9`) and closed seven of the eleven bugs
surfaced by the v0.6.0 walker dogfood. Three actionable items did not make
the v0.6.1 cut and are still costing real time on every walker run; the
v0.6.1 dogfood itself surfaced two new ones, of which the Documenter
CHANGELOG-conflict pattern hit twice on the very release that was meant
to clean up dogfood debt.

This brief drives v0.6.2: a focused patch line that closes the leftover
debt, one more turn of the dogfood crank before any architectural lift.

## Goal

Ship `@cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.2` with three bug fixes that turn the
walker from "drives a substantive Plan to merged with mostly no
hand-rebase" (v0.6.1 reality) into "drives a substantive Plan to merged
with no hand-rebase across CHANGELOG, no time lost to CWD drift, and a
working cross-browser harness on a fresh install." Standard stays at
0.4.1. No new features, no new tracks, no new agents.

## Background

Reference: dogfood debriefs at
`~/.claude/projects/-home-ren-Workspace/memory/cloverleaf-v0.6-walker-dogfood.md`
(the original 11-item v0.6 list AND the appended v0.6.1 retrospective with
items #12 and #13). The three items in scope here are the
cloverleaf-actionable subset; chrome-devtools MCP contention (#5) is
claw-drive territory and stays deferred.

## In-scope bug fixes

Each item below is a candidate task. The Plan agent decides task
granularity and DAG topology — see Open Questions, especially the
parallel-DAG conflict guidance.

1. **`install.sh` does not install system deps for cross-browser playwright.**
   Source: v0.6 walker dogfood (CLV-26, CLV-28). When the cross-browser UI
   Reviewer runs `npx playwright install webkit firefox`, the browser
   binaries are placed but their system shared-library deps
   (`libevent-2.1-7t64`, `libgstreamer-plugins-bad1.0-0`, `libflite1`,
   `libavif16`, `gstreamer1.0-libav`) are not. CLV-28 spent ~30 min
   hand-extracting `.deb` files into webkit's `sys/lib` until the human
   ran `sudo apt-get install`. Fix: `install.sh` detects when the
   cross-browser harness is in scope (probably triggered by an opt-in
   flag, since most consumers stay on chromium-only by default) and runs
   `npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox` with a clear sudo prompt.
   Must degrade gracefully if the user declines (chromium-only path
   continues to work) or if the platform isn't apt-based.

2. **Documenter CHANGELOG conflict pattern.** Source: v0.6.1 walker
   dogfood (CLV-33, hit twice — CLV-34 vs CLV-35 first-merge and CLV-36
   second-merge). When a Plan has multiple tasks and one is the
   version-bump custodian whose DoD includes "bump `package.json` + write
   `## 0.X.Y` CHANGELOG section", Documenter agents in sibling tasks each
   add their own "Unreleased" CHANGELOG entries. These collide with the
   custodian's `## 0.X.Y` section during walker rebase and required `git
   checkout --ours reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md` resolution both times.
   v0.6.1's brief explicitly warned about parallel-DAG shared-file
   conflicts and the Plan agent serialized SKILL.md edits correctly, but
   CHANGELOG slipped through. Fix candidates: (a) Documenter prompt
   detects when a sibling task is the version-bump custodian (via Plan
   inspection — the task list is in the Plan JSON, custodian is whichever
   task's DoD mentions `package.json` version bump or
   `## <version>` CHANGELOG section) and skips CHANGELOG entirely; (b)
   walker rebase step defaults to `--ours` for CHANGELOG when the
   conflict is purely additive; (c) both, as belt-and-suspenders. The
   user-meaningful behavior is: a sibling Documenter never produces a
   CHANGELOG diff that the custodian's section wouldn't already cover.

3. **Session B CWD drift inside walker worktrees.** Source: v0.6.1
   walker dogfood (CLV-33, CLV-36 specifically). CLV-36's Session B
   spent ~30 min in a debug loop because its CWD silently drifted into
   the `standard/` subdir during normal operation (likely from a prior
   `cd standard && npm test`-style step). `git ls-tree HEAD` then
   returned paths without the `reference-impl/` prefix, confusing diff
   inspection and causing Session B to think it was looking at a
   wrong-shaped repo. Eventually recovered without escalation, but the
   30 min was pure waste. Fix candidates: (a) walker passes absolute
   `$WORKTREE_ROOT` to Session B in the scenario brief, and Session B's
   first preflight line is `cd "$WORKTREE_ROOT"`; (b) every agent prompt
   (`prompts/{implementer,documenter,reviewer,ui-reviewer,qa}.md`)
   starts with `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`; (c) both. Note
   that (a) is walker-side (touches `SKILL.md`) and (b) is per-agent
   (touches each agent prompt). They are independent and both cheap.

## Open questions / Discovery hooks

1. **Cross-browser opt-in mechanism.** Most consumers don't need
   webkit/firefox. Should `install.sh` run `playwright install-deps`
   unconditionally (slow + intrusive sudo prompt for users who don't
   need it), or only when invoked with `--with-cross-browser`, or only
   when `.cloverleaf/config/ui-review.json` lists webkit/firefox in
   `browsers`? The config-driven approach is cleanest but means
   install.sh has to read consumer config that may not exist yet. Best
   answer is probably an explicit flag with a clear README note; a
   later release can wire it to config detection.

2. **Custodian detection mechanics for #12.** How does the Documenter
   know a sibling task is the version-bump custodian? The Plan JSON has
   the task list and each task's DoD. The Documenter prompt could
   inspect `context.plan` (loadPlan from the work-item) and grep the
   sibling tasks' DoDs for `package.json` + `version` or `## <version>`
   + `CHANGELOG`. Alternative: the Plan agent emits an explicit
   `version-bump-custodian: true` field on the custodian task during
   `breakdown`, and Documenter just reads that field. The latter is
   cleaner but requires a tiny Standard-touching change (or a
   reference-impl-only annotation in the task's `metadata` field if that
   exists). Defer to spike if needed.

3. **Walker `--ours` rebase default for CHANGELOG.** Even with #12 fixed
   in the Documenter prompt, consumers running an older Documenter
   would still produce conflicts. Should the walker's rebase step (if
   it does a rebase) explicitly use `-X ours` for CHANGELOG by default,
   with a way to opt out? This is a small SKILL.md change. Discuss
   tradeoffs in spike or RFC.

4. **Prompt-prefix retrofit for #13.** If we add `cd "$(git rev-parse
   --show-toplevel)"` to all five agent prompts, that's a five-file
   touch. Each is small but if Plan parallelizes them (they're
   independent text edits) we hit the parallel-DAG issue again. Should
   #13 be a single task that edits all five files together, or
   distributed across per-agent tasks? Single task is simpler.

5. **install.sh testing.** install.sh isn't run by the test suite
   (it's the install entry-point itself). How do we get a regression
   test for the cross-browser flag? Options: (a) shell-mock the
   `playwright install-deps` call and verify it was invoked; (b) a
   smoke test in `scripts/acceptance-*.sh` that runs install.sh in a
   temp dir; (c) just doc-test it. Cheapest is probably (a).

## Parallel-DAG conflict guidance (lessons from v0.6.1)

This release will modify a small set of files. Plan agent: please
infer DAG edges from file overlap, not just from logical dependency.
Files that will be touched and by which conceptual fix:

- `reference-impl/install.sh` — fix #1 only.
- `reference-impl/prompts/documenter.md` — fix #2 only.
- `reference-impl/skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md` — fix #3
  (option a — walker passes `WORKTREE_ROOT`) AND optionally fix #2
  (option b — `--ours` rebase default for CHANGELOG). If both touch
  SKILL.md, those tasks must be **serialized** via DAG edges.
- `reference-impl/prompts/{implementer,documenter,reviewer,ui-reviewer,qa}.md`
  — fix #3 (option b — preflight `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`).
  Note `documenter.md` is shared with fix #2 — those tasks must be
  serialized.
- `reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md` — **version-bump custodian only.**
  Sibling tasks must NOT touch this file. If using fix #2 option (a),
  the custodian's Documenter still adds the `## 0.6.2` section as
  normal; the prompt fix prevents siblings from racing.
- `reference-impl/package.json` — **version-bump custodian only.**

The version-bump custodian should be the **join sink** of the task DAG
(downstream of all bug-fix tasks via edges). It is the ONLY task that
touches CHANGELOG and package.json. If the Plan agent prefers, it can
be a separate "release prep" task downstream of all fixes; if simpler,
it can be one of the bug-fix tasks (probably fix #2's task, since #2
is itself the CHANGELOG-conflict fix and the custodian is its first
user).

The fixes to #12 and #13 in this very release will NOT be active during
the release's own delivery — Session B agents will be running v0.6.1's
prompts and SKILL.md. The only mitigation we control is this brief. The
Plan must make CHANGELOG single-custodian (no Documenter adds an
"Unreleased" entry on a non-custodian task) so we don't hit the bug
during our own release.

## Success criteria

- All three bugs fixed with regression tests in `reference-impl/tests/`
  (or shell-mock equivalents for install.sh).
- v0.6.2 release dogfood (this very Plan) exhibits **#12 NOT recurring**
  — no manual `git checkout --ours CHANGELOG.md` rebase resolution
  required. (Caveat: the fix isn't active during the release itself,
  so this success criterion is enforced by Plan structure, not by
  software change.)
- A subsequent walker run (post-v0.6.2 install) demonstrates #12 and
  #13 fixes are active: a Plan with two parallel tasks where one is
  the version-bump custodian — sibling Documenter does not add a
  CHANGELOG entry, no manual rebase needed.
- Standard stays at 0.4.1. Reference-impl bumps to 0.6.2.
- CHANGELOG entry under `## 0.6.2`.
- Tag `reference-impl-v0.6.2`, GitHub Release published, npm publish.

## Non-goals

- Not addressing dogfood debt #5 (chrome-devtools MCP single-profile
  contention) — claw-drive architecture, separate project.
- Not addressing dogfood debt #8 (DAG-edge inference from shared-file
  modification overlap) — design question for v0.7. The Plan agent
  for v0.6.2 itself still relies on the file-overlap guidance in this
  brief; the systemic fix is later.
- Not introducing the unified `/cloverleaf-flow` orchestrator — v0.7
  scope.
- Not changing the walker's external API (skill name, args, exit
  behavior). Internal skill-body, prompt, and install-script changes
  only.
- Not touching the Standard. Schemas, contracts, conformance harness
  remain at 0.4.1.
- Not retroactively fixing the v0.6.1 release's CHANGELOG conflicts —
  already merged on main with `--ours` resolution; the v0.6.1 section
  is correct.
solution:
Three focused bug fixes ship as @cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.2 with no changes to @cloverleaf/standard (stays at 0.4.1) and no new agents, tracks, or external API surface. The three bugs have non-overlapping primary fix locations that support parallel workstreams, except that documenter.md is touched by both bug #2 and bug #3 and SKILL.md is touched by both bug #2 (walker-side --ours fallback) and bug #3 (walker-side WORKTREE_ROOT injection) — those tasks must be serialized in the Plan DAG.

Bug #1 — Cross-browser system deps (install.sh): Spike CLV-41 confirmed that: (a) npx playwright install chromium webkit firefox already runs unconditionally today (all three browser binaries downloaded); the gap is only install-deps, which covers system shared-library deps; (b) on non-Linux platforms playwright's own installer prints a platform-warning and exits 0 with no system changes, so no additional bash guard is needed; (c) the config-driven approach (reading .cloverleaf/config/ui-review.json) is blocked by a bootstrap problem — consumer config lives in the consumer repo, not available at install time; (d) existing call sites (./install.sh and ./install.sh --project) would not break from an added flag. install.sh gains an explicit --with-cross-browser CLI flag parsed from "$@" at the top of the script. When the flag is present on Linux, the script replaces the current unconditional npx playwright install-deps webkit call with npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox, adding system shared-library deps for both webkit and firefox. When the flag is absent on Linux, the existing install-deps webkit behavior is preserved unchanged. On non-Linux platforms, the install-deps call is a playwright-level no-op regardless of the flag. When the flag is absent the script prints: "(Pass --with-cross-browser to also install webkit/firefox system deps for cross-browser UI review.)". README documents: pass --with-cross-browser when .cloverleaf/config/ui-review.json sets browsers to include webkit or firefox. A shell-mock regression test asserts that install-deps webkit firefox is invoked when the flag is present and that only install-deps webkit (not install-deps firefox) is invoked when absent.

Bug #2 — Documenter CHANGELOG conflict (dual-flag Option B): Spike CLV-42 confirmed Option B is fully viable without any Standard changes. task.schema.json line 73 declares extensions as an explicit optional property referencing extensions.schema.json; its patternProperties regex (^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$) matches both clv.version-bump-custodian and clv.changelog-suppressed; loadTask in task.ts is a raw JSON.parse cast that round-trips extensions intact; cloverleaf-document/SKILL.md step 5 substitutes {{task}} with the full task JSON sourced from cloverleaf-cli load-task, so extensions ARE present in the Documenter's context. Critical gap confirmed by spike: the Documenter receives only its own task JSON (no Plan context, no sibling visibility), so the suppression flag must live on the suppressed sibling task itself (clv.changelog-suppressed), not only on the custodian.

The fix is belt-and-suspenders. Prompt-side (two files): reference-impl/prompts/plan.md gains a ~4-line addition instructing the Plan agent, at breakdown time, to emit extensions["clv.version-bump-custodian"]: true on the custodian task and extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true on each non-custodian sibling. reference-impl/prompts/documenter.md gains a ~6-line preflight block before any CHANGELOG.md edit: if task.extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"] === true, return {"commits_added": 0, "files_changed": [], "summary": "CHANGELOG suppressed: custodian sibling handles version bump and release section."} immediately without touching CHANGELOG.md; if task.extensions["clv.version-bump-custodian"] === true, write the ## <version> CHANGELOG section as directed by the task's definition_of_done rather than an ## [Unreleased] section. Walker-side: SKILL.md's rebase step uses -X ours for reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md as a belt-and-suspenders fallback absorbing conflicts from consumers running older Documenter prompts that predate this fix. Immediate dogfood path (no tooling changes required): a human operator can hand-set extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true directly in the Plan JSON for non-custodian tasks — AJV validates it today, loadTask round-trips it intact, and the Documenter receives it in {{task}}.

Bug #3 — Session B CWD drift: Both sub-options are applied. Walker-side: SKILL.md is updated to embed the absolute WORKTREE_ROOT path in the Session B scenario brief, with an explicit instruction that Session B's first preflight step must execute cd "$WORKTREE_ROOT" before any git command. Prompt-side: all five agent prompts (implementer.md, documenter.md, reviewer.md, ui-reviewer.md, qa.md) gain cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" as their first executable preflight line, anchoring each agent to the worktree root regardless of CWD drift source. Because all five prompts are independent text edits with no shared file outside documenter.md (which T2 already owns), these edits can be batched into a single task to avoid parallel-DAG collisions on documenter.md.

DAG topology: Three parallel root tasks — (T1) install.sh cross-browser fix touching install.sh only; (T2) Documenter CHANGELOG fix touching prompts/plan.md, prompts/documenter.md, and SKILL.md; (T3) CWD drift fix touching SKILL.md and all five agent prompts including documenter.md — converge into (T4) a release-prep join-sink task that is the sole custodian of CHANGELOG.md and package.json. T2 and T3 must be serialized because both touch documenter.md (T2 adds the suppression preflight, T3 adds the cd preflight) and both touch SKILL.md (T2 adds the --ours rebase fallback, T3 adds the WORKTREE_ROOT injection). T1 is independent and can run in parallel with T2 or T3.
acceptance_criteria: install.sh parses --with-cross-browser from "$@" at the top of the script; when the flag is present on a Linux/apt-based platform, npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox is invoked (replacing the current unconditional install-deps webkit-only call).

install.sh without --with-cross-browser on Linux preserves the existing npx playwright install-deps webkit behavior and does not invoke install-deps firefox; the script prints an informational note: "(Pass --with-cross-browser to also install webkit/firefox system deps for cross-browser UI review.)"

install.sh with --with-cross-browser on non-Linux platforms does not fail — playwright's own installer handles non-apt platforms as a graceful no-op (warning + exit 0), so no additional bash platform guard is required inside the flagged branch.

A shell-mock regression test in reference-impl/tests/ (or reference-impl/scripts/) verifies that playwright install-deps webkit firefox is invoked when --with-cross-browser is present and that only install-deps webkit (not install-deps firefox) is invoked when the flag is absent.

reference-impl/prompts/plan.md instructs the Plan agent to emit extensions["clv.version-bump-custodian"]: true on the custodian task AND extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true on each non-custodian sibling task at breakdown time.

reference-impl/prompts/documenter.md includes a preflight block that returns {"commits_added": 0, "files_changed": [], "summary": "CHANGELOG suppressed: custodian sibling handles version bump and release section."} immediately when task.extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"] === true, without touching CHANGELOG.md.

When task.extensions["clv.version-bump-custodian"] === true, the Documenter writes the ## <version> CHANGELOG section as directed by the task's definition_of_done rather than an ## [Unreleased] section.

A regression test verifies the Documenter CHANGELOG-skip behavior: given a synthesized task JSON with extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true, the Documenter produces a result with no CHANGELOG.md entry in files_changed.

reference-impl/skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md rebase step uses -X ours (or git checkout --ours) for reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md when a conflict is detected during walker rebase, as a belt-and-suspenders fallback for Documenter versions predating this fix.

reference-impl/skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md embeds the absolute WORKTREE_ROOT path in the Session B scenario brief with an explicit instruction to cd "$WORKTREE_ROOT" as the first preflight step before any git command.

All five agent prompts (reference-impl/prompts/implementer.md, documenter.md, reviewer.md, ui-reviewer.md, qa.md) include cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" (or an equivalent absolute anchor) as the first executable preflight step.

The v0.6.2 delivery run of this RFC's Plan completes without any manual git checkout --ours CHANGELOG.md rebase resolution — enforced by Plan DAG structure (single join-sink custodian) and by hand-setting extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true on non-custodian tasks in the Plan JSON before the run, rather than by the software fix being active during its own release.

reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md contains a ## 0.6.2 section listing all three bug fixes: cross-browser system deps (#3 from v0.6 dogfood), Documenter CHANGELOG conflict (#12 from v0.6.1 dogfood), and Session B CWD drift (#13 from v0.6.1 dogfood).
@cloverleaf/standard version remains at 0.4.1 and its package.json is not modified.
Tag reference-impl-v0.6.2 is created, a GitHub Release is published with a summary of the three fixes, and npm publish is executed for @cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.2.
out_of_scope: Dogfood debt #5 — chrome-devtools MCP single-profile contention across parallel walker sessions. Claw-drive architecture; not a reference-impl change.

Dogfood debt #8 — DAG-edge inference from shared-file modification overlap. Deferred to v0.7 design; the v0.6.2 Plan itself relies on explicit file-overlap guidance in the brief for human-verified DAG topology decisions.
The unified /cloverleaf-flow orchestrator that fuses Discovery and Delivery. Deferred to v0.7 scope.
Changes to @cloverleaf/standard schemas, contracts, or conformance harness. The Standard stays at 0.4.1 and its package.json is not touched.
New tracks, agents, or skills beyond the three in-scope bug fixes.
API changes to the walker skill: skill name, invocation arguments, and exit behavior are unchanged; only internal SKILL.md prose, agent prompt files, and install.sh change.
Retroactively amending the v0.6.1 CHANGELOG or re-running v0.6.1 release branches. Those conflicts are already resolved on main via --ours and the v0.6.1 section is correct.
A new cloverleaf-cli subcommand for walk-state reconciliation. The --reset flag remains the documented migration path for stale walk-state.json files.
